title: Senior's toolkit: reviewing at scale
summary: ripgrep for the sinks, gh to read a PR's diff, a custom Semgrep rule for your own helpers, CodeQL in code scanning, CODEOWNERS for security-sensitive paths, and threat-model tools.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: reviewing at scale
steps.body: One reviewer cannot read every line of every PR with security eyes. These tools point the eyes at the lines that matter, and make the machine catch the patterns you have already seen once.

toolkit.what: A sinks sweep: every place in a codebase where one of the dangerous APIs from this topic is used, with two lines of context. The fastest first hour of a security review.
Read a pull request's diff in the terminal, then search it for new sinks, new endpoints and new dependencies.
flags: run it locally and attack it

toolkit.what: Your own rules for your own code: once a review finds a bug pattern ("FindAsync on a tenant table without an owner filter"), write it as a rule so the next PR is caught by CI.
flags: what to match, and the safe variants to skip
toolkit.example:
rules:
  - id: html-raw-on-model
    languages: [generic]
    paths: { include: ["*.cshtml"] }
    pattern: "@Html.Raw(Model. ...)"
    message: "Html.Raw on model data: encode it, or sanitize first"
    severity: ERROR

toolkit.what: Taint analysis on every PR through a GitHub Actions workflow: results appear as PR annotations and in the Security tab, with the data flow from source to sink.
flags: more security queries than the default
toolkit.example:
- uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
  with:
    languages: csharp
    queries: security-extended
- run: dotnet build
- uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4

toolkit.what: Make changes to security-sensitive paths require a review from the people who own them: auth, crypto, payment code, CI workflows, dependency manifests.
flags: branch protection: require code owner review

toolkit.cmd: OWASP Threat Dragon / Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool
toolkit.what: Draw data flow diagrams with trust boundaries and get STRIDE threats suggested per element; save the model next to the code so it is updated with the design.
flags: open source, web or desktop, JSON models in the repository
often enough: element, threat, mitigation, ticket
toolkit.example: docs/threat-models/partner-webhooks.json   (Threat Dragon model, reviewed in the design PR)

steps.prompt: Match each tool to its place in the review.
pairs: first hour of reviewing an unfamiliar codebase
reading one pull request in the terminal
making a bug you found once a CI failure forever
source-to-sink paths across methods, on every PR
the security team must approve auth changes

steps.prompt: Search the C# and Razor files for raw HTML and raw SQL, with line numbers and two lines of context.
A review found an IDOR caused by `db.Invoices.FindAsync(id)` on a multi-tenant table. What makes sure the pattern does not come back?
options: A custom Semgrep (or CodeQL) rule in CI that flags FindAsync on tenant tables, plus a regression test with the attack request
A comment in the code asking people to be careful
